name: Santo Mauro, a Luxury Collection Hotel
positioning: Santo Mauro, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Madrid: a French-style palace built for the Duke of Santo Mauro between 1889 and 1902, with three buildings set in a private garden in Madrid's Golden Triangle
best_for: Travelers who want to stay in a historic aristocratic palace with its original interiors
Visitors who want a city-center base close to Madrid's most renowned museums
Guests who value a private garden with fountains and terraces in the middle of the city

facts.text: The palace was built by architect Juan Bautista Lázaro between 1889 and 1902 as a residence for the Duke of Santo Mauro.
The hotel consists of three buildings set in a private garden with fountains and terraces shaded by ancient chestnut trees.
The Red Room reflects French Classicism, while oriental pieces in the Chinese Lounge recall objects the Duke collected on his travels.
The ducal family still owns the palace, acting as its stewards.
The palace is in the Golden Triangle neighborhood, long the center of aristocratic life in Madrid and home to aristocratic residences, embassies and art galleries.
The hotel is in the city center, close to the design area and the city's most renowned museums.
All rooms and suites have marble bathrooms, luxury bedding and high-speed Wi-Fi.
The minibar holds Madrid specialties, including a local wine selected by the sommelier, local pastries and traditional Spanish crisps.
Gresca Wine Bar has a cellar of more than 250 references, including national, international and natural wines.
The signature Casilda cocktail is served complimentary to in-house guests every day.
The hotel offers a walking tour of Madrid's Chamberí district.
The hotel has a fully equipped fitness centre open 24 hours.

highlights.text: The hotel retains its original interior design, including a Modernist staircase in the entrance hall, a small oval courtyard, an old chapel and the Duke's library.
The Duke's Royal Suite was the original Duke's bedroom, with walls covered in green velvet.
The garden was shaped under the guidance of landscape artist Fernando Valero, with fountains and historic trees.
The Luxury Terrace Suite is a bi-level suite with a garden view and a terrace.
The hotel keeps a cabinet of curiosities in the tradition of Madrid's aristocratic collectors.

considerations.text: Pets are allowed but not in the indoor food and beverage outlets.
Rooms at the hotel do not have a fridge.
WhataHotel notes limited room inventory due to the hotel's boutique size.
